battle.name: 第一次英阿戰爭
battle.brief: 一八三九年四月，約二萬一千人的印度軍由基恩率領渡過印度河，四月廿五日駐紮坎大哈，七月廿三日以火藥爆破城門攻下加茲尼，八月入喀布爾扶沙迦复位。卡面輪發手槍是一六〇〇年前後的德意志機括，四百年後只剩火燧手槍還在英軍軍官腰間；左右戰局的卻是火繩傑薩伊、滑膛步槍的射程與三萬頭駱駝的後勤。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 交戰的兩邊不是兩個國家，而是英屬印度與阿富汗兩個政治實體。英方是東印度公司的孟加拉軍與孟買軍：兵員由加爾各答的總督奧克蘭公爵調度，出戰的英籍部隊有第十三索默塞特輕步兵團、第十六槍騎兵團、第二女王團與第四龍騎兵團，公司的團隊有第四十三步兵營、第十九步兵營、斯金納騎兵團、第二輕騎兵營與普納地方騎兵，另有沙迦自掏腰包招募的六千名印度傭兵；全軍約二萬一千人，隨軍人夫與眷屬約三萬八千人。指揮系統是典型的殖民式雙軌，軍事命令經公司參謀處下達，外交與情報歸民政總監威廉·海·麥克納頓。阿富汗一方沒有常備軍，埃米爾杜斯德穆罕默德汗以部落的哈薩一夫制臨時徵召普什圖、塔吉克、烏茲別克與哈扎拉人出戰；杜拉尼舊部在喀布爾與坎大哈另立旗號，加茲尼守軍由穆罕默德·阿富扎爾汗率領，坎大哈則有科恩·迪爾汗兄弟。第三方各有算盤：旁遮普的蘭吉特·辛格以條約換取聯軍光臨喀布爾的權利，俾路支的卡拉特與巴赫特里普什圖各自守土，錫克軍在一八四一年圍困白沙瓦。唯一公開反對英方的是加茲尼城下的加茲萊武裝。
countriesEn: The two sides were not two nations but two political entities: British India and Afghanistan. The British side was the Bengal and Bombay armies of the East India Company: the troops were mustered by the governor-general in Calcutta, Lord Auckland, and the British regiments in the field included the 13th Somersetshire Light Infantry, the 16th Lancers, the 2nd Queen's Regiment and the 4th Dragoons, while the Company's units included the 43rd and 19th Native Infantry, Skinner's Horse, the 2nd Light Cavalry and the Poona Local Horse, with six thousand Indian mercenaries raised at Shuja's own expense. The whole force numbered about twenty-one thousand men, with some thirty-eight thousand camp followers and their families. The command system was the typical colonial double track: military orders travelled through the Company's staff, while foreign affairs and intelligence were the province of the political agent, William Hay Macnaghten. The Afghan side had no standing army. Emir Dost Mohammad Khan called out the tribal levy of the Pashtuns, Tajiks, Uzbeks and Hazaras in the hazara system; Durrani loyalists raised their own banners in Kabul and Kandahar; the garrison of Ghazni was under Mohammad Afzal Khan, and at Kandahar the brothers Kohan Dil Khan held the south. Third parties had their own arithmetic: Ranjit Singh of the Punjab bought the right to appear in Kabul with a treaty, the Kalat and the Baluch Pashtun tribes guarded their own ground, and the Sikh army besieged Peshawar in 1841. The only open opponent of the British was the Ghilzai irregular force under the walls of Ghazni.
people: 英方最具爭議的人是威廉·喬治·基思·埃爾芬斯通少將，他在喀布爾的指揮因拖延與軟弱被記為一八四二年慘敗的關鍵；守傑拉勒巴德的羅伯特·塞爾上校戰死，助理軍醫威廉·布賴登是唯一走回印度的英籍軍人。首席政治官威廉·海·麥克納頓在與阿克巴爾汗會談時被殺，屍體在巴扎被拖行示眾；亞歷山大·伯恩斯在暴動中與家人一同遇害，他的日記是後人重建喀布爾那一夜的主要依據。約翰·基恩爵士率軍完成一八三九年的進軍，亨利·巴納德爵士、喬治·波洛克爵士與威洛比·科頓先後接任；奧克蘭公爵是整盤棋的設計者，威廉·蒙斯圖亞特·埃爾芬斯通則是他在喀布爾的耳目。阿富汗方面，杜斯德穆罕默德汗先在帕爾萬達拉擊敗英軍、退往布哈拉，一八四二年回國复位；其弟穆罕默德·阿克巴爾汗是反攻的策劃者，屢次以山民夜襲與游騎騷擾英軍。沙迦·沙赫在加茲尼下令把被俘者斬首，被英方史官記為野蠻無度；普什圖長老阿卜杜拉·汗·阿查茲伊在喀布爾召開會議宣布聖戰，給了反英勢力第一個名分；加茲尼守將拉赫曼·汗陣亡。旁遮普方面，蘭吉特·辛格自一八三九年六月病重，舒爾·辛格於同年冬季承位，其後錫克軍才在英人要求下自普什圖撤圍。
peopleEn: The most disputed figure on the British side was Major-General William George Keith Elphinstone, whose hesitating command in Kabul became the stock explanation for the disaster of 1842; Colonel Robert Sale, who held Jalalabad, was killed, and the assistant surgeon William Brydon was the only British soldier to reach India. The chief political agent, William Hay Macnaghten, was killed when he met Akbar Khan, and his body was dragged through the bazaar for display; Alexander Burnes and his family were torn to pieces in the mob, and Burnes's diary is the principal source by which the night in Kabul has been reconstructed. Sir John Keane led the advance of 1839, and Sir Henry Barnard, Sir George Pollock and Sir Willoughby Cotton followed in turn; Lord Auckland designed the whole operation, and Mountstuart Elphinstone was his informant in Kabul. On the Afghan side Dost Mohammad Khan defeated the British at Parwan Darra and withdrew to Bukhara before returning in 1842; his brother Mohammad Akbar Khan planned the counter-offensive, troubling the British with night raids by the hill people and long-range harassment by horsemen. Shuja Shah had the prisoners beheaded at Ghazni, which the British official historian recorded as wanton barbarity; the Pashtun elder Abdullah Khan Achakzai called a council in Kabul and proclaimed a jihad, giving the anti-British movement its first cause; Rahim Khan, the defender of Ghazni, was killed. In the Punjab, Ranjit Singh fell ill from June 1839 and Sher Singh succeeded him that winter, after which the Sikh army was made to lift the siege of Peshawar at British insistence.
kits: 卡面這件輪發手槍在戰役裡從未上陣，但它指出了這個時代手槍的技術源頭。十六世紀初德意志的輪發機括以發條帶動棘輪擊打燧石，火星落進藥盤，十七世紀的火燧機由此脫胎，十九世紀的軍官手槍已是火燧式，所以一八三九年英軍軍官腰間那把短管手槍，其實是卡面這件兵器三百年後的樣子。真正交戰的裝備另有其物：英軍步兵用舊式燧發滑膛步槍，裝填慢、射程短、精度有限，刺刀掛在槍口；阿富汗方面的主力是傑薩伊，槍身比英軍步槍長近半，用火繩點火，能居高臨下越過英軍縱隊射擊，這正是加茲尼與坎大哈外圍大量外籍軍官不願正面進攻的原因。炮兵方面，英軍有野戰炮與攻城炮，卻在坎大哈把攻城用的重炮留了下來，攻加茲尼時只能靠火藥炸開城門；喀布爾與坎大哈的阿富汗炮隊則由數名改籍的歐洲軍官訓練，射擊精度不低。運輸完全靠人背獸馱：三萬頭駱駝、數萬頭牛羊，連一個團都帶著獵犬，隨軍人夫多達三萬八千人。山地沒有道路，糧秣、柴薪與傷員全靠馱畜，這條脆弱的補給線才是遠征真正的敵人。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on this card never went into action, but it marks the technical source of the sidearm in this era. The sixteenth-century German wheel lock used a spring-driven ratchet to strike a piece of pyrite and throw sparks into a priming pan; the seventeenth-century flintlock grew out of it, and by the nineteenth century officers' pistols were flintlocks, so the short-barrelled pistol at an English officer's hip in 1839 was in truth the three-hundred-year descendant of the weapon on this card. The arms that actually fought were others: British infantry carried the old flintlock smoothbore musket, slow to load, short in range and poor in accuracy, with the bayonet fixed at the muzzle; the main Afghan arm was the jezail, a gun with a barrel nearly half as long again as the British musket, fired with a match, able to shoot downhill over British columns, which is why so many foreign officers refused frontal attacks around Ghazni and Kandahar. On the artillery, the British had field guns and siege guns but left the heavy pieces behind at Kandahar, so that at Ghazni they could only blow the city gate open with a powder charge; the Afghan batteries at Kabul and Kandahar, on the other hand, were drilled by a handful of European officers who had changed sides and were no mean gunners. Transport was entirely man- and animal-borne: thirty thousand camels, tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, one regiment even brought its foxhounds, and the camp followers numbered thirty-eight thousand. There were no roads in the mountains, and food, fuel and the wounded all travelled on pack animals; that thin supply line, not the enemy, was the real adversary of the expedition.
tactics: 這場戰爭是兩套戰術體系的碰撞。英方行軍自旁遮普出發，四月渡印度河，五月取白沙瓦，六月穿博蘭山口，七月抵達坎大哈，並因要等莊稼熟稔而延誤一個月；攻加茲尼時以爆破組炸開城門，步兵縱隊入城，之後未遇抵抗直取喀布爾。防守方以部落武裝在山嶺與村落之間狙擊英軍縱隊，加茲尼城下的聖戰武裝屢次衝鋒都被壓退，但英方每到一地就沿用同一套城市進攻法，不適應山地的游擊。真正毀掉英方的是佔領之後的做法：營區設在城外無險可守之地，糧秣堡壘破舊而無防，冬季全靠外交維持。撤退的樣子最清楚：一八四二年一月六日全軍離開喀布爾，縱隊走庫爾德卡布爾山口，在寬僅數十碼、積雪兩尺的山道上一路遭吉爾吉武裝襲擊；到甘達馬克時只剩不足四十人，武器只剩十幾支能用的步槍、軍官的手槍和幾把劍，靠方陣與刺刀掙扎。這一段說明：在火繩槍仍守在山地的年代，遠征的勝負由山口與補給線決定，而不是由步槍射程決定。
tacticsEn: The war was a collision between two systems of tactics. The British marched out of the Punjab, crossed the Indus in April, took Peshawar in May, came through the Bolan Pass in June and reached Kandahar in July, then delayed a month more because they waited for the crops to ripen; at Ghazni a demolition party blew the city gate and the infantry entered in column, and after that the advance to Kabul met no resistance. The defenders fought with tribal irregulars sniping from the ridges and villages between the columns, and the jihad fighters under the walls of Ghazni were repulsed time after time, but the British used the same assault on towns everywhere and never adapted to mountain irregular warfare. What destroyed them was what they did after the conquest: the cantonment was pitched outside the walls where it could not be defended, the supply fort was old and half open, and the whole of the winter was left to diplomacy rather than watchfulness. The retreat shows the method most clearly. On 6 January 1842 the column left Kabul, took the Kurd Kabul pass, and was attacked all the way along a road a few yards wide with two feet of snow on it; by Gandamak fewer than forty men were left, armed with a dozen working muskets, the officers' pistols and a few swords, fighting on with bayonets in a square. That passage shows the general law of the period: when the matchlock still held the mountains, the fate of an expedition was decided at the passes and on the supply line, not by the range of a musket.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。英軍主力約二萬一千人，隨軍人夫與眷屬約三萬八千人，駱駝三萬頭，另帶大批牛羊；兵種分屬孟加拉軍、孟買軍與英軍正規團，並有沙迦自募的六千名印度傭兵。加茲尼之戰在一八三九年七月二十三日，英軍傷亡約二百人，阿富汗方面死約五百、被俘約一千五百。英軍大部回印度後，只留約八千人駐阿富汗。一八四二年一月撤退的隊伍約一萬六千五百人，其中作戰人員約四千五百、隨軍人夫逾一萬二千；甘達馬克的最後掩護只剩約四十人，可用武器僅十餘支步槍、軍官手槍與少數劍；一八四二年一月十三日抵達傑拉勒巴德的英籍軍人只有威廉·布賴登一人。全戰英方軍人與隨軍人員死亡約一萬五千至四萬，戰費約兩千萬英鎊。此外，參考條目把開戰時間記為一八三八年十月一日的前後，實際渡河與戰鬥自一八三九年四月開始；參戰團隊的番號、兵站與傷亡數字在不同官方戰史中互有出入，引用時需保留這一點。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The main British force was about twenty-one thousand men, with some thirty-eight thousand camp followers and their families and thirty thousand camels, plus large numbers of cattle and sheep; the troops came from the Bengal army, the Bombay army and British regiments, together with six thousand Indian mercenaries raised by Shuja. The battle of Ghazni was fought on 23 July 1839: British dead and wounded about two hundred, Afghan dead about five hundred and prisoners about fifteen hundred. After most of the army returned to India, only about eight thousand men were left in Afghanistan. The column that withdrew in January 1842 numbered about sixteen thousand five hundred, of whom roughly four thousand five hundred were combatants and more than twelve thousand were camp followers; the last covering party at Gandamak was down to about forty men, armed with a dozen working muskets, the officers' pistols and a few swords; on 13 January 1842 the only British soldier to reach Jalalabad was William Brydon. British soldiers and followers killed over the war are put at fifteen to forty thousand, and the cost at about twenty million pounds. Note also that reference lists date the opening of the war to around 1 October 1838, while the crossing and the fighting began in April 1839; regimental numbers, depots and casualty returns differ between official narratives, and that difference should be preserved when they are quoted.
cause: 動因有三層。最外層是俄英在亞洲的角力：一八三七年英國決策者擔心俄國會借道阿富汗進攻印度，一八三八年俄國使者維特金抵達喀布爾並得到杜斯德穆罕默德汗接納，消息傳到倫敦與加爾各答便被視為生死攸關，傳聞的成本往往比事實更貴。制度層是公司的算計：奧克蘭公爵無法同時與阿富汗和旁遮普結盟，蘭吉特·辛格的軍隊更有紀律也更聽命，公司於是選擇扶植沙迦复位，把巴控的阿富汗變成一個附庸。內政層是阿富汗本身的王位繼承：杜拉尼王系的坎大哈分支與巴拉克扎伊的喀布爾分支爭鬥不休，沙迦據說被劫掠、虐待並致盲，其兄仍在，復辟就成了一切方案裡最便於操作的一個。推動計畫的還有商業與路運：東印度公司要的是通往印度的安全商路，也要一個能被當作緩衝的喀布爾，而不是一個可能被俄國借用的獨立勢力。沙迦在喀布爾的問禮儀式自一八三九年起年年加碼，被英方視為培植傀儡的記號；加上英方需要一個能對外交代的理由，於是有了「恢復合法君主」這個說法，掩蓋了換掉一個難以控制的埃米爾的實質。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause. The outermost was the Anglo-Russian rivalry in Asia: in 1837 British planners feared that Russia would march on India through Afghanistan, and when the Russian envoy Vitkiewicz reached Kabul in 1838 and was received by Dost Mohammad Khan, the news reaching London and Calcutta was treated as a matter of life and death, and rumour always cost more than truth. The second layer was the arithmetic of the Company. Lord Auckland could not ally with Afghanistan and the Punjab at once; Ranjit Singh's army was the more disciplined and the more amenable, so the Company chose to restore Shuja and turn British-controlled Afghanistan into a dependency. The third layer was the Afghan succession itself: the Kandahar branch of the Durrani house and the Barakzai branch at Kabul were locked in conflict, Shuja was said to have been plundered, tortured and blinded, his brother was still alive, and a restoration was therefore the most workable of all the available plans. Commerce and the road pushed the scheme forward as well: the Company needed a safe trade road into India and a Kabul that could serve as a buffer, rather than an independent power open to Russian use. The ceremonial homage paid to Shuja in Kabul was made larger every year from 1839 and was read in London as the sign of a puppet being dressed; and because the British needed a story that would satisfy Parliament, the cause was presented as the restoration of a rightful king, concealing the fact that the real object was to replace an emir who could not be handled.
impact: 後果第一層在軍事與心理：一八三九年的勝利來得太便宜，兩年後的崩潰就格外刺眼；甘達馬克的殘餘成為歐洲與印度共同記住的形象，英國自此認定高山遠征必須以政治手段與後勤科學重新設計。其二在政策：一八四二年諾特與波洛克的增援軍攻入喀布爾，扶杜斯德穆罕默德汗复位，英國放棄沙迦，改走「承認現狀、以資助換取影響」的查謨與克什米爾路線，一八九三年劃下的杜蘭線正是這條路線的終點。其三在國際：英國自認在阿富汗替俄國擋了一道門，此後對中亞的干涉步步升級，一八六〇年代英俄在塔城與帕米爾的角力都以此為前奏。其四在阿富汗：被扶植的沙迦一旦失去英軍撐腰即遭推翻，一八四二年他被殺，一八四六年杜斯德穆罕默德汗病故，家族在喀布爾的命運自此與英國在印度的力量同起同落，一八七九年第二次英阿戰爭時又被推翻。其五在後世的科學與文學：一八四二年的慘敗催生了喜馬拉雅測量與地質考察的長期投入，也讓人重新計算高山醫療、糧秣與馱畜的極限。
impactEn: The consequences came in layers. The first was military and psychological: the victory of 1839 had been cheap, and the collapse two years later was correspondingly grotesque; the remnant of Gandamak became an image remembered across Europe and India, and Britain concluded that any future expedition into the mountains had to be redesigned around political management and the science of supply. The second was policy: in 1842 the relieving armies under Nott and Pollock entered Kabul and restored Dost Mohammad Khan; the British dropped Shuja and took instead the line of recognising the facts of the ground in exchange for subsidies, and the line first surveyed in 1893 was the end of that policy. The third was international: Britain believed it had shut a door against Russia in Afghanistan, and its interventions in Central Asia grew step by step from there, the Anglo-Russian contest at Chuguchak and in the Pamirs in the 1860s being a direct continuation. The fourth fell on Afghanistan: a puppet like Shuja was overthrown the moment British troops withdrew, and he was killed in 1842; Dost Mohammad Khan died in 1846, and from then on the fortunes of the ruling house in Kabul rose and fell with the strength of Britain in India, until the Second Anglo-Afghan War of 1879 threw it down again. The fifth was scientific and literary: the disaster of 1842 drove the long investment in Himalayan surveying and geology and forced a reckoning with the limits of high-altitude medicine, food and pack animals.
result: 結果分三段。前段是一八三九年的軍事成功：七月廿三日加茲尼城破，八月沙迦在喀布爾复位，英軍留八千人駐守；翌年杜斯德穆罕默德汗在帕爾萬達拉打敗英軍、退入布哈拉，一八四一年反攻幾乎把英軍逐出喀布爾。中段是毀滅：十一月二日喀布爾因一樁奴籍糾紛引發暴動，麥克納頓被殺，埃爾芬斯通坐失時機，軍官與士兵在巴爾哈薩與城內街巷被逐次殲滅；十二月英方以「安全通行」換得撤退許可，一八四二年一月六日出喀布爾，十三日只剩布賴登等數人抵達傑拉勒巴德。最後一段是復仇：諾特自坎大哈攻陷加茲尼，波洛克自白沙瓦打通開伯爾山口，聯軍九月重入喀布爾，同年十月十二日戰事以杜斯德穆罕默德汗复位告終，英軍隨即撤出。從兵器看，這場戰爭留下的不是勝負而是兩個教訓：遠征的成敗由糧秣與山口決定，而不是由步槍射程決定；而在火繩槍仍守在山地的年代，遠征真正依靠的是情報、運輸與外交，不是槍。
resultEn: The result runs in three stages. The first was the military success of 1839: the fall of Ghazni on 23 July, Shuja crowned at Kabul in August, and eight thousand British troops left in the country; the following year Dost Mohammad Khan beat the British at Parwan Darra and withdrew to Bukhara, and the counter-offensive of 1841 drove the British almost out of Kabul altogether. The second stage was destruction: on 2 November a quarrel over a servant girl set off a rising in Kabul, Macnaghten was murdered, Elphinstone hesitated, and officers and men were picked off in the Bala Hissar and in the lanes of the city; in December the British bought a safe conduct, and on 6 January 1842 the column left Kabul, of whom by 13 January only Brydon and a handful of others reached Jalalabad. The last stage was retribution: Nott took Ghazni from Kandahar, Pollock cleared the Khyber from Peshawar, the combined force re-entered Kabul in September, and on 12 October the war ended with Dost Mohammad Khan restored, after which the British withdrew. Judged by its arms, the war left behind not a result but two lessons: the fate of an expedition is decided by supply and by the passes, not by the range of a musket, and in an age when the matchlock still held the mountains, what carried a distant expedition was intelligence, transport and diplomacy, not gunfire.
